label: topic: one_variable_data
result:
All 9 grid-in templates in one_variable_data now carry `spr_mistakes`. The work is one commit on `v2/t-bank-one_variable_data`, not pushed and not merged.

BRANCH: `v2/t-bank-one_variable_data` (from `v2/t-bank` @ 9403838), in worktree /Users/workingmyassof/satbank/.claude/worktrees/wf_c70c4702-929-13

COMMITS
- `fda18d1` "Name the mistakes behind a wrong grid-in in One-Variable Data"

FILES CHANGED (13 lines added, 9 removed; `kit.py` not touched)
- /Users/workingmyassof/satbank/.claude/worktrees/wf_c70c4702-929-13/satbank/topics/one_variable_data/families/basic.py: the grid-in branch of `_finish`
- /Users/workingmyassof/satbank/.claude/worktrees/wf_c70c4702-929-13/satbank/topics/one_variable_data/families/means.py: the grid-in branch of `_num_item`
- /Users/workingmyassof/satbank/.claude/worktrees/wf_c70c4702-929-13/satbank/topics/one_variable_data/families/freq.py: the grid-in returns of `freq_stat` and `freq_two_groups`
- /Users/workingmyassof/satbank/.claude/worktrees/wf_c70c4702-929-13/satbank/topics/one_variable_data/families/boxes.py: the grid-in return of `box_read`

Each of those grid-in returns now ends with `spr_mistakes=gridin_mistakes(key, mistakes)`. Nothing had to be moved: every template here already built its `mistakes` list before the grid-in branch. No rng draw and no call that can raise changed place.

TEMPLATES COVERED (9 of 9)
- `ovd.list_stat`, `ovd.table_stat` (the `pair_sum` case included) and `ovd.bar_read`, all through `_finish`
- `ovd.unknown_value` (the `equal_means` and `integer_mean` modes), `ovd.mean_totals` (`removed` and `combined`) and `ovd.mean_identity` (`consecutive` and `fraction_of_sum`), all through `_num_item`
- `ovd.freq_stat`
- `ovd.freq_two_groups` (the `median_difference` case)
- `ovd.box_read`

TEMPLATES LEFT, AND WHY
- None of the grid-in templates is left.
- These 10 templates never produce a grid-in, so there is nothing to add: `ovd.freq_order`, `ovd.freq_choose`, `ovd.compare_sets`, `ovd.sd_compare`, `ovd.measure_effect`, `ovd.odd_measure`, `ovd.new_data_set`, `ovd.box_compare`, `ovd.reason_center`, `ovd.must_be_true`. Their options are sentences built by `assemble_text`, or the item hard-codes "mcq".
- Two paths inside covered templates also stay multiple-choice only, because the item hard-codes "mcq": `unknown_value`'s `mean_equals_median` mode and `reason_center`'s `median_interval` mode.
- `freq_two_groups`'s `compare_means` case is also multiple-choice only; its options are sentences.

EVIDENCE
- **Before/after dump:** I ran the given script for seeds 0-60 with no `fmt`, `fmt="mcq"` and `fmt="spr"`, on the base commit and again after the edit. `diff` of the two outputs is empty across 3,477 lines covering all 19 templates (1,633 multiple-choice, 588 grid-in). So multiple-choice items are unchanged, and grid-in items differ only in `spr_mistakes`.
- **Quality gate:** `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m satbank check --topic one_variable_data` prints PASS. Every check is ok, including audit (5,700 items re-derived), which now enforces the `spr_mistakes` rules.
- **Coverage:** `PYTHONPATH=. python3 tools/spr_coverage.py` now reports "9 of 202 grid-in templates name their mistakes", with `one_variable_data` at 9 of 9 (it was 0 of 9).
- **Spot check (seeds 0-60, grid-ins only):**

| Template | Grid-ins | Without mistakes |
|---|---|---|
| `list_stat` | 79 | 0 |
| `table_stat` | 61 | 0 |
| `bar_read` | 61 | 0 |
| `freq_stat` | 61 | 0 |
| `freq_two_groups` | 20 | 0 |
| `box_read` | 61 | 0 |
| `unknown_value` | 52 | 0 |
| `mean_totals` | 73 | 0 |
| `mean_identity` | 122 | 0 |

- **What an entry looks like:** in `mean_identity` with key 1/8, the wrong answers are 8 ("reported the number of values"), 1/7 and 1/9.

Two things behave in ways you might not expect:
- **Negative values:** some named wrong values are negative, for example −8 in `mean_totals` ("swapped the two counts"). It is a real result of the template's own logic, so it was kept.
- **`box_read` list:** its grid-ins use the same list as its multiple-choice options. That list has already dropped any wrong value sitting too close to another on the axis.
